headline: Single-cell model claims depend on evaluation thresholds and data support
label: Model Validity In Omics Learning
summary: Stricter retention thresholds and uncertainty scoring expose where single-cell and multi-omics model outputs lack adequate support.
synthesis: The dominant thread is whether model outputs in single-cell and multi-omics analyses are supported by the data and evaluation behind them. SABLE-MO shows that stricter retention thresholds reduce false acceptance of shared and private factors in simulations and TARGET/TCGA cancer data, while latent-factor stability alone is found insufficient. Optimal-transport soft couplings score per-cell match uncertainty, improving label transfer and integration. A mass cytometry study reports LLM-based cluster annotations reaching 85-98% metacluster concordance, within the range where human experts disagree. scOmnom pairs scalable end-to-end scRNA-seq analysis with BISC-based clustering-resolution selection and auditable linked outputs. The spliced/unspliced NMF work addresses latent model specification rather than validity directly. What is new is treating evaluation thresholds, match uncertainty, and annotation agreement as part of the model claim rather than reporting accuracy alone.
